title: Judge Orders Release of Canadian Dentist Held in Minnesota
summary:
A Canadian dentist detained by United States immigration officers in Minnesota is back home after a federal judge ordered his release.

Dr. William Lizardo, 32, was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, known as ICE, on October 23 and held at Sherburne County Jail. He was ordered removed from the United States. On Sunday evening, hours after the judge's order, he was finally released, his lawyer Hassan Ahmad confirmed.

U.S. District Judge Michael J. Davis wrote that Lizardo's arrest and detention violated his constitutional rights. The judge called the facts "appalling," noting that Lizardo filed changes of address each time the couple moved, and that USCIS communicated with him at each new address.

Lizardo moved to the United States on a student visa in 2019 to study at the University of Minnesota School of Dentistry. He graduated in 2023, married an American that same year, and later had a daughter. His wife's petition for an alien relative, filed in 2023, was approved in January 2025.

In January, his request for permanent residency was denied because he had failed to provide a certified document from Ontario. Orders to appear at later hearings were sent to the wrong address, so Lizardo missed them and was then arrested.

Lizardo asked to have the removal order rescinded because he had never received the hearing notices. An immigration court granted that request on October 28, finding he had provided sufficient evidence of lack of notice. ICE argued he should be kept in custody while the green card case was being decided, but the judge ruled agents had no reason to believe he was a flight risk and ordered him immediately released, saying he simply wanted to make sure Lizardo did not spend another night in jail. Lizardo is now waiting for a USCIS decision on his green card application.
why_it_matters: The case shows how a wrong address can change a person's life, and why courts check whether detention is fair before someone is kept in custody.

background_read: A green card is a document that allows a person from another country to live and work permanently in the United States.
To get one, applicants often need to show documents, attend hearings, and wait for immigration officials to decide their case.
If hearing notices go to the wrong address, a person can miss a hearing without knowing about it, which can lead to serious problems.
A judge can order a person to be released if detention breaks their rights or if there is no good reason to keep them in custody.
